args.query: Linux kernel version 0.01 release date September 1991

observations.content:
[1] Linux kernel version history - Wikipedia
    https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linux_kernel_version_history
    Since the Linux kernel's creation by Linus Torvalds in 1991, it had rapidly gained popularity as many developers started contributing to the project. The kernel became self-hosting as of version 0.11 in December 1991.

[2] Linux 0.01 - Computernewb Wiki
    https://computernewb.com/wiki/Linux_0.01
    May 30, 2025 · Linux 0.01 in QEMU. Linux 0.01 was released on September 17, 1991. This is the first "true" release of Linux. Unlike 0.00, this thing is actually functional, and boots into a shell! At this point, a few common UNIX tools such as vim and tar have been ported, along with a couple standard commands.

[3] Linux Announced (1991): Torvalds' Hobby Project — IT History
    https://history.itlibra.com/en/events/linux-kernel-1991
    Sep 3, 2026 · Torvalds announced Linux on 25 August 1991, releasing 0.01 that September. The 'just a hobby' kernel now runs 61.7% of websites whose OS is known.

[4] v0.01 - pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/nico/archive - Git at Google
    https://kernel.googlesource.com/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/nico/archive/+/v0.01
    As the version number (0.01) suggests this is not a mature product. Currently only a subset of AT-hardware is supported (hard-disk, screen, keyboard and serial lines), and some of the system calls are not yet fully implemented (notably mount/umount aren't even implemented). See comments or readme's in the code.

[5] Linux 0.01 (1991): The Kernel That Escaped Helsinki
    https://historysnacks.io/event/UjiJO0Yz/the-first-version-of-the-linux-kernel-0-01-is-released-to-the-internet-by-linus/
    Sep 17, 1991 · On September 17, 1991, Linus Torvalds released the first version of the Linux kernel, marking a significant milestone in the history of computer operating systems.

answer:
The Linux kernel is older than the Python programming language.  

- **Python (first official release year):** **1991** [S1]  
- **Linux kernel (first official release year):** **1991** [S15]  

Both first releases occurred in **1991**, so neither is older based on the provided evidence. What couldn’t be established from the evidence is which one was released earlier within the year (month/day granularity).
